FOR E W 0 R D
0.1 This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 2_5 January 1974, after the draft finalized by the Terminology; Notations and Drawings Sectional Committee had been approved by the Civil Engineering Division Council. 0.2 Tais standard was first issued in 1967. In this revision provisions with regard to the variation" in the height of the seat of chair and finish have been incorporated. This standard also makes reference to the recent Indian Standards on materials of construction.

0.3 In the formulation of this standard due weightagc has been given to international co..ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in this country. . 0.4 This standard contains clauses 2.1.1 and 2.1.5 which permit the purchaser to use his option for selection to suit his requirement. 0.5 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS: 2-1960�. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as tha t of the specified value in this standard. �

I. SCOPE
1.1 This standard specifies functional requirements for

chairs for

draftsmen for use with drafting tables. 2. RECOMMENDATIONS 2.1 Chairs shall be light in weight so that they can be easily moved to facilitate the draftsman's movements relative to the drawing board or reference surface. The chair shall be designed to permit the feet to be
-Rules for rounding off numerical values (.rnristd).

placed under it easily and comfortably when desired. For freedom of sidewise movement of the draftsmen, the chairs shall not be provided with band rests.

2.,1.1 Height of Slilt - The seat height shall be 620 mm from the . floor to top of the seat. The scat may be provided with a vertical axle for swivelling to mise or lower the height of the seat up to 150 DUn, if so desired by the purchaser. 2.1.2 Elfleti", Dlpth of SIllt - The effective depth of the seat shall be not less than 350 mm and shall not be more than 400 mm. This shall be measured from the point on the seat where the midpoint of the backrest extended vertically downwards meets the seat, to a vertical plane touching the front edge of the seat. . 2.13 St", S"'flJU - The scat surface shall be horizontal and may be cushioned, caned, moulded out of plastic or made out of wood or similar suitable material.
2.1.4 Width ofS,Ill- The width of the scat in the front and back shall be not less than 400 mm and 350 mm respectively (sle Fig. 1 ).

2.1.5 Btdrut - The following are recommended:
a) The backrest shall be padded or caned. The angle of slope fixed with respect to the leat surface being 95 to 100 degrees. The backrest may be made adjustable . with a slope of 95 to 110 degrees, if 10 desired by the purchaser. b) The depth of the backpad�shaJl be 150 mm.
c) The width of the ~pad .hail be not more than 350 mm.

d) The backpad aba1l be . curved in the horizoDtal plane with a radius of not lea than 300 mm and preferably 400 to 450 DlDl. (

e) The distance frO~ the leat surface to the bottom of the backpad sha11 be a4justable between ISO to 250 IDID. .
f) Padding of backrests is required (or cOmfort and C accommodation � to dimcmioDl.

shall be used.

5. SAFETY
5.1 All exposed parts of the framework shall be smooth or rounded to minimize the risk of damage to the clothing or person or the user. 5.2 The seat section shall be secured to the leg section be detached inadvertently.

6. LEGS

6.1 Legs and the framework shall be adequate to support the user in any position which he may be required to assume in the course of his work. Ends of legs shall be fitted ~ith shoes of rubber, plastic, or any other resilient material to prevent sliding. 7. :A~LJiI.::': 7.1 The metal drafting chairs shall be assembled by means of welding. 7.1.1 For mild steel, parts the method of gas, and arc welding shall conform to IS: 1323-1966� and IS : 816-1969t. 7.1.2 Aluminium parts shall IS : 2812-1964:. be welded

8. FINISH

8.1 Metal CompoDeDt.
8.1.1 All dents, burn and sharp edges shall be removed from the components and they shall be pickled, scrubbed and rinsed to remove grease, rust, scale or any other foreign clement. 8.1.2 After pickling, all the mild steel parts shall be given phosphating treatment in accordance with IS: 3618-196611 followed by a coat of suitable primer, such as red oxide.

b) Finish coat with synthetic stoving enamel conforming to IS: 2932-1964� or IS : 2933.1964t, and c) The components shall thereafter be baked at a specified temperature in an oven heated uniformly. The finish shall be smooth and uniform with a hard and tough film of enamel strongly adhering to the surface. The finish shall be free from all visible defects and shall not chip when taped lightly with a poinsed instrument. .

8.2 WoodeD Components - The wooden components may be polished either with wax polish or a transparent glossy french polish or stained dark and polished. .
9. PACKING

9.1 All the component parts shall be packed in such a way that no damage is caused to them during transit.

10. INFORMATION TO BE SUPPLIED BY THE PURCHASER
10.1 The purchaser shall supply the following information to the
supplier along with the order: . a) Material of construction for chair and seat, b) Colour and finish. and

c) Whether the seat is to be provided with an arrangement for its variation in height or not.
